channel.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
channel.description: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

item.title: Cost of living has gone up 3.4% in the last year
item.description: A new report shows the cost of living in August was up 3.4% from a year ago. Investors think stubborn inflation makes it more likely that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week.
item.content:encoded: A new report shows the cost of living in August was up 3.4% from a year ago. Investors think stubborn inflation makes it more likely that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week.
item.dc:creator: Scott Horsley

item.title: Yemen's Houthis say they now control land that overlooks a key shipping route
item.description: Yemen's Houthis have overrun Saudi-backed forces to consolidate control along a Red Sea shipping strait.
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Houthis have overrun Saudi-backed forces to consolidate control along a Red Sea shipping strait.

item.title: Ethics watchdogs await RFK Jr.'s financial report
item.description: Health Secretary RFK Jr.'s annual financial disclosure is late. When it posts, the public could learn how much he has earned from a vaccine-related lawsuit against Merck, which RFK now regulates.

item.title: What it takes to make a new — branded — tomato
item.description: Why is the grocery store produce aisle filling up with branded fruits and vegetables, like honeycrisp apples and cuties oranges? We watch the effort to make one new — branded — tomato.

item.title: The other side of 9/11: Afghans reckon with America's long shadow
item.description: It's been nearly 25 years since the start of the U.S- led invasion of Afghanistan. NPR returns to Kabul to see how Afghans, now back under Taliban rule, are coping with the legacy of that 20 year war.

item.title: Rubio visits new right wing governments in Latin America
item.description: The shift to the right in Latin America is reshaping the U.S. approach to drug trafficking — a shift on display this week as Secretary of State Marco Rubio traveled to three South American countries.

item.title: For swing voters in Michigan, Trump's Canada tariffs feel personal
item.description: Swing voters in Michigan are sour on the economy — and President Trump's handling of it. That's one takeaway from a pair of focus groups this week.

item.title: An Oregon nonprofit harvests fruit from backyards and parks for people in need
item.description: In the Portland area, one nonprofit harvests edible fruit from thousands of metro trees, shrubs and bushes and distributes it to people in need.

item.title: Mayor of the 'Air Capital of the World' reacts to Trump's threats against Bombardier
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks with Wichita Mayor Lily Wu about President Trump's tariff war with Canada, Bombardier aircrafts, and the trade war's potential impact on her city.

item.title: The intelligence community changed after 9/11. Where is it now?
item.description: The 9/11 terrorist attacks changed the nation's approach to national security. NPR's May Louise Kelly speaks with four U.S. officials about the intelligence community's response and where we are now.
